brief: Goldman's weekly cross-asset credit recap for Nov 3-7: equities sold off sharply (S&P -2.7% on the week, -4.4% intraday Thursday) after the Democratic midterm sweep, but credit barely moved (IG 1bp wider, HY 4bps tighter, loans best week since April), so credit absorbed the shock without confirming the equity-implied move. Record IG issuance ($76bn, nearly double expectations) was dominated by hyperscaler financing ($67bn, pushing YTD hyperscaler issuance to $296bn), while chip CDS overtook hyperscaler CDS in spread terms for the first time in three months as AI financing risk migrates toward chips. Beneath calm index levels, dispersion is widening: HY AI bonds underperformed generic HY by over 2 points, distressed loans below $80 nearly doubled, and the 2028 maturity wall looms for weaker issuers. Tony Pasquariello argues 2027 is less rewarding given slowing EPS growth, the largest net supply increase since 2000, and deepening negative hyperscaler free cash flow, and says contacts think equities look too sanguine relative to credit. Midterm data-center policy risk (state moratoria touching ~45% of planned capacity) is framed as stretching the AI buildout cycle, not shrinking its addressable market.
